summary: Milestone 2026.05.250 completed 0 experiments in 0 minutes of wall time — the twenty-fifth consecutive empty-timing-window retro. No compute-bound tasks ran (gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks is null per the GPU idle interpretation rule). The planning phase was productive: 13 tasks (exp2608–exp2620) were drafted, gate-audit-passed, and the root cause of the 25-milestone execution drought was confirmed as the sklearn-blocked chain (exp2596/2597/2600 all returned blocked_sklearn), which exp2609 is queued to fix.
bottlenecks_identified: Structural planning-execution gap: milestones complete well-formed planning (13 tasks, gate-audit-passed, prior_failures complete) but the conductor does not activate any experiment before the retro trigger fires — 25 consecutive milestones with zero execution commits.

sklearn not installed in the conductor Python environment: exp2596 (tier0s retrain), exp2597 (tier0u fix), and exp2600 (safety corpus) all returned blocked_sklearn, blocking the entire retrain dependency chain for 25+ milestones.

Timing-script look-back may not be anchored to conductor-state.json activation timestamp: if the look-back window predates experiment commits, those commits are invisible to the retro, causing artificially empty timing reports even when experiments did run.
improvements_suggested: Activate exp2609 (scikit-learn install + sklearn precondition fix) in the same session as milestone planning — this single task unblocks exp2610, exp2611, and exp2613, which together form the AUROC recovery chain.

Fix the timing-script look-back to use the conductor-state.json `activated_at` timestamp as its lower bound, not a fixed rolling window, so future retros capture all experiments that actually ran within the milestone.

Gate the retro trigger on minimum_experiments_completed >= 1: if the trigger fires with 0 experiments, emit a lightweight 'planning-only' stub and defer the full retro until at least one experiment has committed.
Deploy a persistent conductor daemon (long-running process, not per-session invocation) to eliminate the structural gap between planning sessions and experiment activation.

Add a post-planning activation step to the conductor's milestone-close sequence: after writing research-roadmap-next.yaml, immediately activate the first non-blocked task rather than waiting for the next conductor session.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: IMMEDIATE: Activate exp2609 (scikit-learn install) same-session as this retro — it is the single-point unblock for the entire exp2610→exp2611→exp2613→exp2615→exp2616→exp2619 dependency chain; resolving it converts a 25-milestone drought into a functioning execution pipeline.

SHORT-TERM: Fix timing-script look-back to anchor to conductor-state.json activation timestamp — this eliminates the false-empty retro pattern that has consumed turn budget across 25 milestones without providing actionable data.

STRUCTURAL: Deploy persistent conductor daemon so experiments activate immediately after planning without requiring a separate conductor session — removes the single largest source of the planning-execution gap.
meta_reflection: Twenty-five consecutive empty-timing-window retros represent a systemic process failure at the execution layer, not at the planning layer: roadmaps are well-formed, prior_failures blocks are complete, gate audits pass — but no experiments activate before the retro fires. The sklearn fix (exp2609) addresses the immediate content blocker, but closing the structural gap requires either same-session activation discipline or a persistent conductor daemon. Until one of those structural changes lands, each milestone's retro will continue to report 0 experiments regardless of plan quality.
